findings.summary: The day-pack sprite is a long body with a top loop and two straps that leave the shoulders and run down beside it, ending in light tips. At 1x it reads as an apron or a sleeved smock as much as a backpack, and it sits close to the coat in the next row.
The key-ring sprite is a ring on a long diagonal shaft with barely visible teeth. Its outline reads as a wand or a dipper more than a key.

notes: SCOPE: screen step, 1 sample of each app (20261019-032024). Every gate passes (eval-1.md). Palette consistency is 0.917, type consistency 1 and reference spacing overlap 0.893. The smoke tests are not run at this step. The harness measured no layout defects, so there was nothing to confirm or dismiss. Light and dark captures are identical because the system is dark only. Known capture gap, not penalized: the settings plan-dialog scrim ends at about 900px in the full-page capture.

REGRESSION CHECK vs critic-1 on 1.3.0-rc.2: its one major (garment sprites lost the outline that names them) is FIXED. On the sweater (drawings/home-d8.png and the detail page products-merino-crew-sweater-desktop-dark.png), the sleeves leave the shoulders and angle out to cuffs that sit clear of the body. The coat (home-d4.png) has sleeves angling away from the shoulders, a collar and a button placket, so it reads as a coat, not a vest or columns. The tee keeps its spread sleeves (home-d12.png). Compared with published 1.2.0 (1.2.0-rc.9 s2 home-desktop-dark.png), the garments read at least as well, and every sprite is now larger in its window.

Earlier minors are not re-raised. Some are still visible: the skillet reads as a magnifier, the towels read as two documents with tabs instead of a bag, the blog hero action is an outlined button, and the settings and dashboard sidebars stop above the ground strip.

UPDATE GOAL (generalization, 1.3.0 with the rc.2 size fix and the rc.3 silhouette fix): REACHED in this sample. Result counts are plain captions ('Showing 11 products', 'Showing 6 of 6 posts', 'Showing 8 of 8 projects'). Block meters appear only against real maximums: uptime, the bio limit (42/160) and the free-shipping threshold in the cart summary. Each kind of screen has its own scene: a catalogue strip, a shared detail banner whose sign word changes by category (BAGS, WEAR), a cart strip, a shared article banner and a settings banner signed per section (USER, BILL). The chart and activity panels end level. The KPI tiles are one row of four. Nothing is worse than the published version.

Two-column layouts: on product detail the picture column ends about 150px above the purchase column, and on the cart the items column ends about 125px above the checkout window. Both are under the spec's 160px limit. Not a finding.

SIGNATURE (4): present in all four apps and placed as Applying the concept says. That means the full-bleed blog hero with a moon, a lit lead building with a sign, a stepped path and a hill (blog home-desktop-dark.png vs reference p1-desktop-light.png), a banner or strip per kind of screen, an inline article figure, the framed vignette on empty results (dashboard state-empty-filter), the checkered ground strip on every route, the gold marker and the hue top bars. Motion is stepped: nc-bob loops at 1000ms with steps(1) on the product banner (motion-products-merino-crew-sweater-m1.png). The item sprites read in 9 of 11 cases. The two weaker ones are listed as minors.

OTHER SCORES. Fidelity (4): the night ground, cream pixel type, 4px windows, dithered rules under h2s, hard-shadow gold commits and hue bars, as in reference p1-desktop-light.png, without copying its cabin, figure or snow. Hierarchy (4): the scene and h1 come first, then 48px KPIs and prices. States (4): the first invalid field gets a gold focus frame and the rest get danger frames with '!' messages (commerce state-checkout-errors). The plan dialog is a titled window with Cancel and a gold Confirm. Empty filter results show a vignette and a framed Clear filters action. Spacing (4) and polish (4): controls that share a row share one height, radius is 0 and no browser defaults are left over.
VERDICT INPUT: no blocker and no major. Two new minors are listed once. The candidate passes the screen and can go on to the confirm step.
